new.pl: NE NW sec. 14 T52N R34W, Houghton County, west shore of Otter Lake
new.v: Coins, tokens, logging-camp tools, bottles, buttons
new.st: The 1911 Houghton County plat book (T52N R34W page) prints "Sherman's Camp" on the west shore of Otter Lake, just below the sec. 11/14 line, with the Old Road running along the shore past it. The 1954 USGS Pelkie topo still draws the shore road there, with a few buildings beside it. The pin sits on the shore at the plat's position.
new.t: Look for a level camp clearing between the shore road and the lake, with old bottles, stove parts and horseshoes. Ask the landowner first.
src: Plat book of Houghton County, Michigan (Weston & Hancock, c1911), T52N R34W page (UMich scan 29; Neb's screenshot)
pinev: Placed from the 1911 plat label against the 1954 Pelkie topo shore road and section line; good to about 150 m
Unconfirmed, one source

new.n: "Old Camp Site", sec. 19 T53N R34W (1911 plat)
new.pl: sec. 19 T53N R34W, Houghton County, on the Old Road
new.v: Coins, tokens, logging-camp tools, bottles, buttons
new.st: The 1911 Houghton County plat book marks an "Old Camp Site" with building squares on the Old Road in sec. 19 T53N R34W, so the camp was already abandoned by 1911. The 1954 USGS Pelkie topo shows the section inside the Baraga State Forest, with old woods roads but no buildings. The pin is at the section centre until the plat's exact spot is read.
new.t: State forest land: check the Michigan state forest rules before you detect. Look for the camp clearing along the old road, with bottles, stove parts and horseshoes.
src: Plat book of Houghton County, Michigan (Weston & Hancock, c1911), T53N R34W page (Neb's screenshot)
pinev: Placed at the section centre; the camp can be anywhere in the section, up to about 800 m away
Unconfirmed, one source
